title: Graph Cycle Detection and Topological Sort
question: How would you detect if a directed graph contains a cycle (for instance, detecting circular dependencies in a build system)? Explain the algorithm.

rubric.name: problem_clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies directed vs undirected graph, disconnected components, and graph representation (adjacency list).

rubric.name: algorithmic_choice
rubric.description: Explains DFS with 3-color visiting state (unvisited, visiting, visited) or Kahn's algorithm (indegrees).

rubric.name: time_space_complexity
rubric.description: States O(V + E) time and O(V + E) space for adjacency list and recursion/indegree tracking.

rubric.name: edge_case_handling
rubric.description: Addresses disconnected subgraphs, self-loops, and empty graphs.

rubric.name: communication_clarity
rubric.description: Articulates call stack traversal or queue processing step-by-step.

expected_signals: Explains why simple visited boolean set is insufficient for directed graph cycle detection
Uses recursion stack set / visiting state for DFS or indegree counting for BFS (Kahn's)
Ensures all vertices are checked to cover disconnected components
red_flags: Uses undirected graph cycle detection logic (simple visited parent check) on directed graph
Provides incorrect complexity, e.g. O(V * E)
follow_up_prompts: If a cycle is detected, how would you print the exact vertices participating in that circular dependency?
How does Kahn's algorithm (BFS indegree method) differ from DFS when building a build order sequence?
